question: Students read a passage, then either re-read it or were tested on it. A week later, who recalled more?
answer: The tested students. In Roediger and Karpicke's experiment, students who took recall tests remembered more a week later than those who re-read the passage several times, though re-readers did better after five minutes and felt more confident about their learning.
move: Trust what you can recall unaided over what merely looks familiar.
trap: Re-reading feels like progress because the text looks familiar.
reference: Roediger and Karpicke, Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention, Psychological Science, 2006
